---
title: "TD: The `output/NXS_TCA_corpus/` folder layout"
format: gfm
---

Map of everything the pipeline writes under `output/NXS_TCA_corpus/`, what
each dataset is, and — in detail — how the two combined score datasets
(`scores_combined` vs `scores_combined_ta_ref`) differ.

Everything is a **hive-partitioned Arrow dataset**: directories named
`key=value/`, so `arrow::open_dataset(<root>)` reads the whole tree and
synthesises the partition keys as columns. Partition **values are
URL-encoded** — `%20` = space, `%28s%29` = `(s)`, `%205.1` = ` 5.1` — so
`chapter=Chapter%205.1` is the chapter tag `"Chapter 5.1"`.

## Tree

```
output/NXS_TCA_corpus/
├── zotero/     assessment={tca,nxs}/ chapter=<C>/ part-0.parquet   raw Zotero items
├── ids/        assessment={tca,nxs}/ chapter=<C>/ part-0.parquet   DOI → OpenAlex id
├── corpus/     assessment={tca,nxs}/ chapter=<C>/ part-0.parquet   full snapshot records
├── keypaper/   key_works.parquet  (+ key_works.xlsx)               flat: the 62 definitions
├── embeddings/ config=SPECTER2_runpod/
│   ├── source=corpus/   variant={title,abstract,title_abstract}/ assessment=<a>/ chapter=<C>/ part-*.parquet
│   └── source=keypaper/ variant={title,abstract,title_abstract}/ part-*.parquet   (flat)
├── scores/                 config=…/ variant={title,abstract,title_abstract}/ pairwise-cosine.parquet
├── scores_combined/        config=…/ assessment=<a>/ chapter=<C>/ pairwise-cosine.parquet
├── scores_combined_ta_ref/ config=…/ assessment=<a>/ chapter=<C>/ pairwise-cosine.parquet
└── topics/                 config=…/ bertopic=<name>/ variant=…/   (BERTopic outputs)
```

## Partition scheme per stage

| Dataset | Partition keys | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `zotero`, `ids`, `corpus` | `assessment` → `chapter` | two assessments (`tca`, `nxs`); `chapter` from Zotero tags |
| `embeddings` **corpus** | `config` → `source` → `variant` → `assessment` → `chapter` | carries `chapter`; one leaf per `(variant, assessment, chapter)` with its own `.embed_complete` marker |
| `embeddings` **keypaper** | `config` → `source` → `variant` | flat leaf — keypaper is a single file, no `assessment`/`chapter` |
| `scores` (original 3) | `config` → `variant` | one flat `pairwise-cosine.parquet` per variant; feeds the existing viz layer |
| `scores_combined`, `…_ta_ref` | `config` → `assessment` → `chapter` | mirror the corpus; **no `variant` level** (one combined score per work) |
| `topics` | `config` → `bertopic` → `variant` | empty until BERTopic runs |

## Stages in detail

- **`zotero/`** — raw items downloaded from the two IPBES Zotero assessment
  groups (`download_zotero_assessment()`). One row per item per chapter tag;
  items with no chapter tag land in `chapter=No Chapter`.
- **`ids/`** — the DOIs from `zotero/` resolved to OpenAlex work ids via the
  live API (`get_ids_from_dois()`).
- **`corpus/`** — full OpenAlex records pulled from the local snapshot for
  those ids (`get_corpus_from_snapshot()`), plus a Zotero fallback: items
  with a title + abstract in Zotero but no OpenAlex match are kept with
  `id = "zotero:<KEY>"` and `record_source = "zotero"`.
- **`keypaper/`** — the 62 TCA/Nexus definitions from
  `TCA and Nexus Definitions.csv`, standardised by
  `prepare_key_definitions()` into `id/title/abstract/…`. A single flat
  parquet (+ an `.xlsx` copy). This is the *reference* set every score is
  measured against.
- **`embeddings/`** — SPECTER2 vectors (768 dims, `V1…V768`) from the TEI
  server, for both the corpus and the keypapers, in three text variants:
  - `variant=title` — title only.
  - `variant=abstract` — abstract only (works with no abstract are dropped).
  - `variant=title_abstract` — `title [SEP] abstract` (works with **no
    abstract are dropped**, so this variant covers fewer works than `title`).

  Corpus embeddings mirror the corpus's `assessment/chapter` partitioning
  (each partition embedded and consolidated independently — see
  `embed_works()`); keypaper embeddings are a single flat leaf per variant.
- **`scores/`** — the original per-variant scoring (`score_keypapers()`):
  cosine similarity of every corpus work against every keypaper, one wide
  `pairwise-cosine.parquet` per variant (`id` + one column per keypaper id).
  These feed the current visualisation layer.
- **`scores_combined/`, `scores_combined_ta_ref/`** — the two combined,
  chapter-partitioned score datasets. Covered next.
- **`topics/`** — BERTopic (UMAP + HDBSCAN) cluster assignments and the
  definitions projected into that topic space.

## `scores_combined` vs `scores_combined_ta_ref`

Both are produced by `score_keypapers_combined()` and are **identical in
shape**: one score per corpus work against each keypaper, partitioned
`config / assessment / chapter`, one `pairwise-cosine.parquet` per chapter.
They exist alongside (not instead of) the original `scores/` triple.

### The shared idea: one score per work, with a fallback

The `title_abstract` embedding is the richest, but it only exists for works
that **have** an abstract. To get a single score for **every** work, each
work is scored from:

- its **`title_abstract`** embedding if it has an abstract, else
- its **`title`** embedding (the *fallback*, for works with no abstract).

This is the same primary + fallback pattern the BERTopic targets use
(`emb_corpus_title_abstract` + `fallback_corpus = emb_corpus_title`).

### The only difference: which keypaper reference the fallback works use

The two datasets differ **only** in which keypaper embedding the *fallback*
(no-abstract, title-only) works are compared against. Abstract-having works
are scored identically in both.

| Corpus work | `scores_combined` | `scores_combined_ta_ref` |
|---|---|---|
| **has** abstract | `title_abstract` vs keypaper **`title_abstract`** | `title_abstract` vs keypaper **`title_abstract`** |
| **no** abstract (fallback) | `title` vs keypaper **`title`** | `title` vs keypaper **`title_abstract`** |

- **`scores_combined`** — *like-for-like*. A title-only work is compared to
  the keypapers' title-only vectors, so both sides of every cosine live in
  the same embedding space. Fallback reference: keypaper `title`.
- **`scores_combined_ta_ref`** — *always title_abstract reference*. Every
  work — including the title-only fallback works — is compared to the
  keypapers' `title_abstract` vectors. One consistent reference across the
  whole dataset, at the cost of a mixed-space cosine (title-only work vs
  title+abstract keypaper) for the fallback rows.

Concretely: rows for works **with** an abstract are byte-for-byte the same in
both files. Rows for works **without** an abstract carry different similarity
values (same `title` corpus vector, different keypaper reference vectors).

### Which to use

- Prefer **`scores_combined`** when you want each similarity to be a clean
  same-space comparison.
- Prefer **`scores_combined_ta_ref`** when you want a single fixed reference
  space for the whole corpus (e.g. to rank all works on one consistent
  `title_abstract` yardstick), accepting that title-only works are then
  compared across spaces.

### Reading them

```r
library(arrow); library(dplyr)

# whole dataset — assessment + chapter appear as columns
sc <- open_dataset("output/NXS_TCA_corpus/scores_combined") |> collect()

# one chapter only (partition pushdown — reads just that folder)
open_dataset("output/NXS_TCA_corpus/scores_combined") |>
  filter(assessment == "tca", chapter == "Chapter 1") |>
  collect()
```

Columns: `id`, one numeric column per keypaper id (from
`keypaper/key_works.parquet`), plus the synthesised `assessment` and
`chapter` partition columns.

## Note: NXS chapter tags are fragmented

`chapter` comes straight from the Zotero tags, and the two assessments are
not equally tidy:

- **`tca`** — clean: `Chapter 1`–`Chapter 5` + `No Chapter`.
- **`nxs`** — fragmented: `Chapter 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7`, `No Chapter`, **and**
  `Chapter 5.0`–`Chapter 5.6` plus a malformed `Chapter(s) 5`. So NXS
  "Chapter 5" is scattered across ~9 partitions.

Every dataset below `zotero/` inherits this fragmentation (one partition per
distinct tag). If "Chapter 5" should be a single unit, normalise the tags
upstream in `zotero_item_to_row()` (collapse `Chapter 5.x` / `Chapter(s) 5`
→ `Chapter 5`); the whole tree then re-derives cleanly.
